representative_questions.question: How does the ethyl acrylate (EA) content in the MMA-co-EA copolymer affect the cell density of the resulting SAN28/MMA-co-EA (50/50 wt%) nanofoams?
representative_questions.expected_answer: Increasing EA content from 0.4% (MMA-EA1) to 5.6% (MMA-EA6) increases cell density (from 3 x 10^14 to 4.0 x 10^15 cm^-3), but further increasing EA content to 12% (MMA-EA12) leads to a decrease in cell density (to 6.9 x 10^14 cm^-3).
representative_questions.why_kept: Only question of this type; no merge

representative_questions.question: Why was a postfoaming (PF) annealing step performed after the initial rapid depressurization?
representative_questions.expected_answer: To avoid uncontrolled changes in cell dimensions and fracturing of the foam samples caused by high residual levels of CO2 trapped at high pressure, which plasticize the polymer matrix and create high internal stresses.
representative_questions.why_kept: Only question of this type; no merge

representative_questions.question: What is the relationship between CO2 solubility in the polymer blends and the resulting cell density of the nanofoams?
representative_questions.expected_answer: Blends with lower CO2 solubility gave higher cell density nanofoams, suggesting that maximizing CO2 solubility does not provide maximum nucleation density.
representative_questions.why_kept: Only question of this type; no merge

representative_questions.question: What effect does increasing the ethyl acrylate (EA) content in MMA-co-EA resins have on the cell size and density of SAN28/MMA-co-EA (50/50 wt%) blends?

representative_questions.question: How does the composition of SAN28/MMA-EA9 blends, specifically the weight percentage of SAN28, affect the resulting cell density and average cell size of the nanofoams?
